questions.question: Isobars are smooth curves connecting all points with equal:
A high-pressure cell usually delivers still, clear, settled weather because:
options: Air inside it SUBSIDES — and subsiding air is compressed, warms, and holds tighter to its moisture, so cloud dissolves

questions.question: Isobars crowded close together on the chart mean:
options: A steep pressure gradient — strong wind
The chart is out of date

questions.question: A station circle shaded seven-eighths reports:
options: All but one okta of the sky clouded — a heavy grey ceiling with a single tear of blue

questions.question: Air temperature 21 °C with a dew point of 18 °C means:
options: Only three degrees of cooling separate this air from saturation — very humid air with condensation close at hand

questions.question: A wind shaft flying into the circle from the north-west carrying one full feather and one half feather reports:
options: A north-westerly at 15 knots — full feathers count 10 knots and half feathers 5

questions.question: Winds are always named for:
options: The direction they blow FROM — their origin

questions.question: On the chart, a cold front is drawn as a bold line set with:
options: Solid triangles mounted on the side the front is advancing toward

questions.question: South African cold fronts characteristically arrive from the:
options: South-west, slung beneath a depression passing south of the continent

questions.question: A wall of cumulonimbus builds along the front line because:
options: Lightning attracts cloud to the line
The triangles on the chart generate storms
The denser cold air rams underneath the warm moist air and pitches it violently upward, forcing rapid cooling and condensation
The sea breeze meets the land breeze there

questions.question: Which station reading is the classic PRE-frontal signature ahead of a South African cold front?
options: Cold south-westerly wind with rising pressure and clearing skies
Hot, dry north-easterly with an empty sky
Warm north-westerly flow, a dew point crowding the temperature, and cloud thickening toward overcast

subtopics.title: The Weather Behind the Front — and the Exam Method

questions.question: The post-frontal trio describing weather behind a cold front is:
In a table of hourly observations, the clearest single marker that the front has passed a station is usually:
options: The wind swinging from north-westerly to south-westerly
The cloud increasing to eight oktas

questions.question: After the front passes, pressure at the station:
options: Climbs, as the depression moves off east and the next high builds in

questions.question: 'Write observations, not impressions' means an answer should:
options: Describe how the weather made people feel
Use as many adjectives as possible
Quote values, name directions and state pressure tendencies — measurable facts a station could report

subtopics.title: Highs, Lows and Which Way the Air Is Going

questions.question: In a high-pressure cell the vertical traffic of air is:
options: Slowly downward — subsiding, compressing and warming

questions.question: The bicycle pump growing warm and the deodorant can turning cold demonstrate that:
options: Compression heats a gas and expansion chills it — which is why sinking air clears the sky and rising air makes rain
Pumps and cans are poorly made
Pressure has no effect on temperature

questions.question: Wind on the pressure landscape is best pictured as:
options: Air climbing from the L up into the H
Air running downhill from the high ground of the H toward the hollow of the L — fast where the isobar slope is steep

questions.question: The two-word summaries of the pressure cells are:

subtopics.title: The Little Circle That Holds a Whole Weather Report

questions.question: Slicing the sky into eight pieces like a milk tart, a station with seven cloudy slices shades its circle:
options: Seven-eighths — nearly the whole tart, one strip of blue left

questions.question: A steel farm gate strung with dew at sunrise shows that overnight:
options: Rain fell only on the gate
The cold metal chilled the air touching it below its DEW POINT, so the air let go of its water
The gate absorbed water from the soil

questions.question: A station reporting 28 °C with a dew point of 6 °C is experiencing:
options: Bone-dry air — twenty-two degrees of cooling would be needed before any condensation begins

questions.question: Winds carry the name of their birthplace because:
options: The chart has no space for destinations
Wind directions change too fast to track
Origin tells you character — a north-westerly over the winter Cape has crossed warm wet ocean and arrives loaded with moisture

subtopics.title: Before, During and After the Cold Front

questions.question: The cold air slides UNDER the warm air 'like a spatula under a pancake' because cold air is:
options: Denser and heavier than warm air, so it refuses to blend and drives in beneath

questions.question: Interrogating the three instruments, a station reporting a raw south-westerly wind tells you the front:
options: Has already been through — the post-frontal wind blows off the cold sea

questions.question: Which set of readings says 'brace for the front — it is still coming'?
options: North-westerly, warm and humid, barometer falling

questions.question: After sweeping the Cape, the same cold air typically reaches the interior plateau:
options: Never — fronts dissolve at the coast
About a day or so later, arriving as the cold snap that has the Free State reaching for jerseys
